evals.prompt: Quick edit this CTA section without changing the offer: 'Ready to take your business to the next level? Our team of dedicated professionals is standing by to help you achieve your goals. Click here to learn more.'
evals.expected_output: Makes a concise clarity and specificity edit, preserves the unknown offer details rather than inventing a value proposition, and explains whether the CTA destination needs confirmation.
assertions: Uses a quick, bounded pass rather than all seven sweeps
Removes cliché and filler where possible
Does not invent benefits, proof, or a new offer
Keeps the meaning boundary visible

evals.prompt: Improve this testimonial: 'CloudSync is great. It really helped our company. - John S., CEO.' No customer interview or additional metrics are available.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the testimonial can be edited for clarity but cannot be made more specific without the customer’s authorised words or evidence; proposes questions or a labelled template instead of fabricating results.
assertions: Preserves attribution and scope
Does not invent a percentage, company size, or outcome
Flags the proof limitation
Suggests a safe next evidence step

evals.prompt: Refresh this old feature page. It says our product supports 20 integrations, but the product team has not confirmed today’s number. Keep the page’s audience and offer unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Uses a refresh pass, preserves the audience and offer, marks the integration number for verification or substitutes safely, and does not silently add new claims.
assertions: Checks factual freshness
Does not repeat the stale number as confirmed fact
Preserves the editing contract
Identifies the required source check

evals.prompt: Review only the proof and specificity of this pricing paragraph. Do not change its overall tone or structure.
evals.expected_output: Runs only the requested proof/specificity checks, flags unsupported numbers or broad claims, and keeps its suggestions within the stated boundary.
assertions: Does not force emotion, risk-reversal, or a full conversion review
Checks attribution and scope for material claims
Preserves tone and structure unless an edit is needed for claim safety

evals.prompt: Write fresh homepage copy for our new CRM for real-estate agents.
evals.expected_output: Routes to copywriting because no existing source copy is being edited; it does not pretend that a copy edit is sufficient.
assertions: Recognises a fresh draft rather than an edit
Names copywriting as the owning capability
Does not create a full page draft within the editing route

evals.prompt: Tighten this services page, but change it so we appeal to enterprise buyers instead of independent founders and introduce a new premium offer.
evals.expected_output: Separates the requested line edits from the new audience/offer decision and routes the strategic part to expert-positioning or product-thinking before presenting it as an ordinary edit.
assertions: Names the audience and offer change
Does not silently make the strategic decision
Routes the decision to the appropriate owner
May provide limited wording alternatives only when labelled as proposed strategy
